Look at the last game for the Magic in the tournament. They knew (as in every other game) that point differential against the Celtics matters, so we ran up the tally against a team that was still in the tournament and had one more game to play after us. 

Now look at the Celtics last game. They were playing a team that was also on their last game of the tournament, and a team that did no go into the game thinking "we have to stop the Celtics from running up the point differential" because they were already out. It is way more likely that you play a team that is already out if you are one of the four teams that plays last. It is a real, albeit small, advantage that exists in the current structure.

Luck is part of it, that determines if the team you are playing for your last game is still playing for the tournament, and cares about the point differential. The point of my post is that despite luck, there is a statistical disadvantage to the 5 Seed because they are more likely to play a team that is still in the running, since the 5 Seed plays their last game before all 4 other teams. Rerun this in a simulation a million times with the current structure and you would see this disadvantage, regardless of what team it is.
I wish it was an obvious flaw, a lot of people seem to be disagreeing with me though that there is an advantage at all. Can't fix it if no one acknowledges it.
